command:change=$(find openspec/changes -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d ! -name archive)
review="$change/review-specs.md"
added=$(git log --diff-filter=A --format=%H -- "$review" | tail -1)
base=HEAD
[ -z "$added" ] || base="$added^"
touched=$({ git diff --name-only "$base"; git ls-files -o --exclude-standard; } | sort -u | grep -vxF "$review" | grep -v '^\.gnomish-task/' || true)
[ -z "$touched" ] || { echo "$touched"; echo "the review-specs stage writes nothing but $review - restore the files above with: git checkout $base -- <file>"; exit 1; }

findings.message: R5 is not real as stated: design.md:19 (D4) says the registry component is wrapped in a factory at registration time. That factory holds the loader, so a registry-side lazy wrapper can create a fresh lazy(loader) on each remount and retry by bumping the boundary key without changing ViewDefinition. The Problem's claim that 'neither ViewHost nor a wrapper can import the chunk again' and the Impact's claim that the ADR-0005 contract must otherwise change are wrong. R5's Fix adds `loadComponent` to the ViewDefinition contract documented in accepted ADR-0005 (docs/adr/0005-view-registry.md:30-37). Its own Fix risk says the ADR must then be amended, which .claude/rules/adr.md forbids for accepted ADRs, so the fix costs more than the gap. A contract-preserving fix (spell out a registry-side retrying lazy factory in views/) should be proposed instead.

R4's Impact says 'The first storage access in the codebase bypasses the port pattern', but packages/client/src/i18n.ts:30-34 already writes the language to localStorage directly through the language detector, as R3 itself cites.

Missed WARNING: design.md:25 (D6) and tasks.md:19 (task 3.1) put strings under three-level `views.cards.*` keys, which contradicts .claude/rules/i18n.md ('flat two-level namespacing: domain.specificKey') and the existing locale structure (`app.*`). No finding covers it.
